NextItNet’s residual causal dilated convolutions capture dependencies over interaction positions; dilation does not itself encode elapsed time ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163)). Searches found related spatiotemporal dilated-convolution work for POI recommendation, but no clearly established 2024–2026 time-conditioned NextItNet variant matching this proposal. Recent evidence supports investigating intervals: [E-NSDE, NeurIPS 2024](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/7cdbd53dfbcf9a5263227555aac5b9cd-Abstract-Conference.html) models continuous-time preference evolution and interval-dependent uncertainty; [TALE, WSDM 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) uses timestamp-based interval weighting and trend-aware normalization; [IntervalLLM, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23209) distinguishes identical item histories with different interaction gaps. These are supporting mechanisms, not evidence of gains for NextItNet on the specified Amazon benchmark.

A family-preserving experiment, inferred from this literature: condition each causal convolution tap on log-scaled elapsed time between its source and destination events, using a small jointly trained gate initialized near identity. Compare ordinary NextItNet, position-only gates, and elapsed-time gates under identical training and validation settings. Include a flexible gate alongside monotonic learned decay: long gaps can indicate uncertainty or periodic interests, rather than universally obsolete history. Preserve an ungated residual path and use only timestamps observable in each prefix; never use the next target’s timestamp. Distinguish interval sensitivity from concept-drift adaptation—interval modeling alone does not establish the latter. All temporal features should remain internal to the single category network, with matching predictor serialization and final-nonpadding readout.
